children: SpiceJet has said it will publish its overdue financial results by 7 December after the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) warned that trading in the cash-strapped airline's shares could be suspended over delays in regulatory filings.

The airline said on Friday that the completion of its audit had taken longer than expected, resulting in the delay in filing its financial statements. A SpiceJet spokesperson told Reuters that the company would meet the exchange's deadline but did not provide further details on the audit delay.

In a notice issued on Monday, the BSE said it would suspend trading in SpiceJet shares from 10 December because the airline had failed to submit its financial results for the quarters ended March and June 2026.
The suspension can be avoided if the airline complies with listing requirements to the exchange's satisfaction by 7 December.
The BSE also warned that during any suspension period, shares held by SpiceJet's controlling shareholders, along with other securities in their demat accounts, would be frozen.

SpiceJet Chairman and Managing Director Ajay Singh is among the airline's controlling shareholders. He held a 12 per cent personal stake as of 31 March, while the wider promoter group owned 24.2 per cent, according to the company's latest available shareholding disclosure.
The latest filing delay comes as SpiceJet continues to face financial difficulties that have weakened its position in India's domestic aviation market.

The airline's market share has fallen to around 0.6 per cent from nearly 15 per cent in 2019. It has reduced flight operations, grounded aircraft and delayed salary payments to several pilots amid a cash crunch.
The airline has also sought government-backed financing to support its operations.
Its financial pressures have been compounded by the conflict in the Middle East, which has pushed up aviation fuel prices and restricted access to certain airspaces, adding to operating costs.
SpiceJet competes with IndiGo and the Air India group, which together accounted for more than 90 per cent of India's domestic passenger market in September.
The airline last reported its financial results in February, posting a consolidated net loss of Rs 262 crore (USD 27.8 million) for the October-December 2025 quarter.

Under Indian listing rules, companies are required to submit quarterly financial results within 45 days of the end of each quarter, except for the final quarter of the financial year. Audited annual results must be filed within 60 days of the financial year's end.
SpiceJet also said it had received an extension from the Registrar of Companies to hold its annual general meeting for the financial year ended March 2026 by 31 December.
Board To Consider Fresh Capital Raising

Separately, SpiceJet said its board would meet on 18 November to consider raising additional capital. The proposed fundraising could involve the issuance of equity shares, debt securities or other financial instruments. The airline has not disclosed the amount it intends to raise.
The proposed capital infusion could provide additional financial support as SpiceJet seeks to stabilise its operations and address its mounting financial challenges.
